title: Field experiment rollout slate and variant watchlist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working slate for running a small-scale field experiment rollout of the new routing/variant logic (v2 routing heuristic + lightweight prefix cache). The goal is to validate latency and quality tradeoffs under live traffic before a broader phased rollout.

Scope & hypothesis:
- Surface-level: route 3% of traffic through the v2 routing path and a quantized variant (q4) behind a feature flag.
- Hypothesis: v2 routing reduces cold-start tail latency by ~25% for 8k+ sequence requests without materially increasing per-token cost when prefix caching engages.
- Risk: regression in hallucination rates for some prompt categories; small risk of increased GPU mem pressure leading to OOMs on rare spike.

Quick decisions to make before scheduling:
- Finalize routing config snapshot id: routing-config-2027-02-10-a (locked)
- Variant mapping: baseline->model-1.3, routing-v2->model-1.3-v2, quantized->model-1.3-q4

Preflight checklist (must be green before deploy):
- [ ] All unit/integration tests for routing components pass (PR #995 green)
- [ ] Canary job run in staging for 48h with synthetic traffic profile A (8k sequences)
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, KV cache hit ratio, GPU mem assignments enabled and validated
- [ ] Alert: paging threshold for 95th perc latency > 800ms for production traffic defined
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed and assigned (see Rollback & emergency section)
- [ ] Legal/privacy check: no PII transformations changed; audit logging enabled for private deployments

Rollout calendar (2-week window) - high level:
- Day 0 (Mon) 09:00 PST: Feature flag flip for 0.5% traffic -> monitoring + watch team on-call
- Day 0 12:00 PST: Evaluate first 3-hour window signals; if no anomalies, increase to 1.5%.
- Day 1 09:00 PST: Increase to 3% if stability OK. Run 6-hour focused sampling for long sequences.
- Day 3: Run surge sim (see Surge scenarios) during low-traffic window to validate autoscaler behavior.
- Day 7: Decision checkpoint: continue ramp to 10% or rollback. Collect evals and human review for top-20 prompt classes.
- Day 14: Publish release notes and postmortem; snapshot metrics and toggle permanent config if rollout succeeds.

Surge scenarios to simulate (ops-runbook commands included):
- Scenario A (gradual increase): +2x traffic sustained for 30m.
  - Trigger: /scripts/surge-sim --scale 2 --duration 00:30
  - Expected: autoscaler spin up + prefix cache warm hit ratio increase; no OOMs in <5% hosts
- Scenario B (spike): +8x for 5m followed by step down.
  - Trigger: /scripts/surge-sim --scale 8 --duration 00:05 --profile spike
  - Expected: graceful degradation: route fallback to baseline for latency-critical paths, fallback log events emitted
- Scenario C (tail-length stress): 10% of requests with sequence>16k for 2h
  - Expected: routing-v2 maintains lower tail latency due to optimized kernel selection; watch GPU mem and KV evictions

Metric gates (simple, machine-checkable):
- Gate 1 (safety): 95th perc latency for production routes must not increase >10% vs baseline for the 6h rolling window.
- Gate 2 (quality): hallucination proxy (classifier false-positive rate) must not increase by >3 percentage points over baseline on sampled prompts.
- Gate 3 (cost): per-token spend must not increase >8% over baseline for the 24h window.
- Gate 4 (stability): no OOM spikes > 0.1% of instances; if hit, auto-rollback.

Variant watchlist (manual & automated):
- variant-routing-v2: watch metric set: [route_lat_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit, cold_start_rate]. Owner: Liam O'Connor
- variant-quantized-q4: watch metric set: [token_quality_score, embedding_consistency, per_token_cost]. Owner: Jordan Rivera
- variant-experimental-sentinel: internal-only, canary mapping for edge prompt categories; watchlist for hallucination classifier score drift. Owner: Sana Iqbal

Communication & channels:
- Primary Slack channel: #release-ops (subscribe: @oncall-release, @eng-qa)
- Incident channel (if gate fails): #release-ops-incident (page flow)
- Standup cadence: 30 min quick check-ins at 10:00 and 16:00 PST for Day0-Day3.

Rollback & emergency steps (short):
1) If Gate 1 or Gate 4 trips: flip feature-flag to baseline via console (feature-flags.redwood/flip -> baseline).
2) If Gate 2 trips (quality): route 100% of affected prompt classes to baseline via topical routing override in routing-console -> profile "quality-protect"
3) Post rollback: take a retention snapshot for all KV caches and logs, open an immediate postmortem ticket (ENG-xxxx) and tag @release-lead in Slack.

Release notes draft (to ship if replicable signals across 7 days):
Title: Incremental rollout: routing-v2 + q4 quantization (limited experiment)
Summary: We launched a 3% field experiment testing the routing-v2 heuristic (improved kernel selection for long-context requests) plus a q4 quantized variant for cost comparison. Early telemetry shows ~18-28% reduction in cold-start tail latency for long-seq requests and a 6% reduction in per-token compute spend when quantized caching engages.
What changed (user-facing):
- No immediate user-visible changes; this is behind a feature flag and routed only for a subset of requests.
- Developers may see slightly faster completions for some long-context flows.
Known issues / caveats:
- A small set of prompt classes (internal tag: finance-calcs, multi-step-code) are flagged for manual review due to slight score drift in generation quality.
- We observed minor memory pressure on a handful of legacy GPU types during surge testing. Workaround: degrade to baseline routing automatically.

Post-rollout to-dos (owners):
- [Anika] Collect final 7-day metric snapshots and prepare an abbreviated exec note.
- [Liam] Run human evals on top-20 prompt classes and summarize precision drift in PR-995 follow-up.
- [Jordan] If quantized variant continues to look good, prepare a Dedicated-config proposal for q4 profile.
- [Sana] Schedule a 60-min retro with SRE and Applied-ML; include dataset samples for hallucination classifier tuning.

Appendix: useful quick links and ops commands
- Staging canary dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/staging-canary
- Production telemetry: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/prod-routing-v2
- Rollback CLI: rwi ops featureflag revert --id routing-v2 --to baseline
- Collect traces: rwi telemetry collect --ids {trace-range} --output /tmp/routing-traces.zip
- Note: when toggling flags for private deployments, coordinate with infra@ to synchronize KMS tokens.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Do we want a staggered ramp tied to region (start US-west -> EU) rather than global percent? Pros: localizes blast radius; Cons: increases rollout duration.
- Should we enable automatic model-variant fallback (if mem pressure) or always prefer explicit rollback? Current plan: automatic fallback to baseline for latency critical routes, manual rollback for quality regressions.

End of slate. Keep this doc as the single source of truth for the experiment until Day14; after that we move an audited copy to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234) if we flip to permanent rollout.
